newsitem.title: POLAND: No danger now of huge new Polish floods -president.
newsitem.headline: No danger now of huge new Polish floods -president.

text.p: Weather reports now suggest there is no danger Poland will face a full rerun of the disastrous floods of the past two weeks, President Aleksander Kwasniewski said in Warsaw on Saturday.

"There is no danger of such a wave (of floods), of such water as we remember a week ago," Kwasniewski told reporters after meeting Poland's central crisis committee as new rains drenched southern and western areas that were just recovering from the earlier deluge.
The rains, falling throughout Friday and into the weekend, earlier sent already-devastated communities back on to disaster alert and a few reported they were starting to be flooded anew.

But flood crisis committee officials said latest forecasts showed the rains on Poland were unlikely to remain very heavy and would shift to the less endangered centre of the country or cease by Sunday.
"It is raining, but less than we expected. Rivers are high but it is not the kind of state we experienced on July 9, 10, 11," Kwasniewski said, stressing this was the situation at 1200 GMT.

He said that unless something very unexpected happened he would not declare a state of emergency in affected areas and these would be able to recover sufficiently for Poland to hold its parliamentary elections as planned on September 21.
